note: Per-CROP-TYPE harvest-readiness attributes. Keyed by crop_types.slug (NOT by variety — cf. lambda/daily-plan/cadence-data-v2.json which is variety-keyed watering/care and is a different key space). This file is the authoring source of record for migrations/v4-harvattr-001/0b-data.sql; the DB columns on crop_types are the runtime source of truth. NULL/omitted attribute = UNKNOWN, and a readiness predicate MUST NOT fire on it. Never substitute a default.

field_contract.harvest_habit: single | repeat | cut_and_come_again. single = one terminal harvest per planting; repeat = discrete fruits picked over a season; cut_and_come_again = the plant regrows the harvested tissue.
field_contract.repeat_interval_days: peak-season days between picks. NULL when harvest_habit='single'.
field_contract.loss_horizon_hours: hours from 'ready' until quality is materially lost if unpicked (on-plant hold, not post-harvest shelf life).
field_contract.set_to_first_pick_days: days from fruit set to first pickable fruit. Only meaningful for fruit-set crops; NULL for leaf/root/bulb crops where status='fruiting' is not the readiness signal.
field_contract.harvest_season_start_doy / harvest_seaso: day-of-year window, set ONLY where harvesting OUTSIDE the window is actively harmful or physically impossible. Deliberately NULL for crops whose window is merely typical — a wrong window SUPPRESSES a true readiness signal, which is the same class of harm inverted.
field_contract.confidence: high | medium | low — authoring confidence. 'low' values are flagged in the coverage report and should be treated as provisional.
field_contract.harvest_tracked: false = deliberately NULL-seeded (ornamental / houseplant / non-fruiting in this zone). Present only on the exclusion list.

pepper.notes: 50-55d set -> full-size green; a further 14-21d to red/colored. Holds on the plant well, hence the long loss horizon. Slug covers BOTH sweet and hot peppers; C. chinense super-hots run longer to colored (add ~7-14d).

tomato.notes: set->pick is size-dependent: cherry ~30d, slicer ~45d, beefsteak/large heirloom ~55-60d. 45 is a mid-population estimate across Dave's 44 plantings (mixed cherry/slicer/beefsteak/paste). Ripe fruit splits after rain; cherry types split fastest.

tomatillo.notes: Ready when the husk splits/fills. Drops to the ground when over-ripe; ground-drop fruit is still usable, so the loss horizon is forgiving.

eggplant.notes: Pick at glossy skin; dull skin = seedy and bitter. 3-5d cadence in peak.

okra.notes: Fastest-turning crop in the set. Pods go woody in 48-72h past ready; miss two days and the pod is inedible.

cucumber.notes: 2-3d cadence. An oversized fruit left on the vine suppresses further set — the loss is to the whole plant, not just the fruit.

cucamelon.notes: UNCERTAIN. Little zone-5b data; extrapolated from cucumber with a slower cadence for the small fruit size. Pick at grape size; larger fruit turns sour.

bitter_melon.notes: UNCERTAIN. Extrapolated from cucurbit relatives. Pick while green and firm; the fruit splits and reddens quickly once mature.

squash.notes: SEEDED AS SUMMER SQUASH. Both live plantings are summer types (Dark Green Zucchini, Zephyr). The crop_types vocabulary has ONE 'squash' slug covering summer AND winter squash, which are horticulturally opposite (winter squash is harvest_habit='single', a ~50d set->pick, and a months-long cure/hold). See flags: a winter_squash slug split is required before any winter type is planted, or this row is actively wrong for it.

melon.notes: Muskmelon/cantaloupe/charentais. 'single' per fruit and effectively per planting in zone 5b — the short season yields one concentrated flush. Slip stage (stem detaches at light pressure) is the readiness signal, not calendar.

watermelon.notes: No slip cue — readiness is the dried tendril + ground-spot color. Over-ripening on the vine is slow, hence the long horizon. Zone 5b is marginal; 45d set->pick assumes a short-season variety.

bean.notes: Snap bean. 2-3d cadence; pods go stringy and the plant stops setting if left to fill seed. NOT currently planted — seeded because the slug exists and the values are high-confidence.

pea.notes: Snap/snow pea cadence. Shelling peas turn starchy fastest. NOT currently planted.

broccoli.notes: Main head first, then side shoots every 5-7d for weeks. set_to_first_pick is NULL by design: the head is a flower bud, not a fruit set — status='fruiting' is not the readiness signal here. Bolts to yellow flower in 2-4d of heat once the beads loosen.

cabbage.notes: One terminal head. Holds in the field for weeks in cool fall weather; splits after heavy rain once mature, which is the real loss event and is weather-triggered rather than time-triggered.

kohlrabi.notes: Pick at 2-3in; goes woody if left much past size. Modern varieties hold better than the 2-week estimate suggests.

collard.notes: Bottom-up leaf harvest, 7-10d. Improves after frost. Very forgiving — old leaves toughen but the plant is not lost.

lettuce.notes: Leaf-lettuce cadence. Bolts bitter fast in July heat; the 48h horizon is a heat-season figure and is conservative in spring/fall.

arugula.notes: Bolts and turns hot/pungent within days in summer heat.

endive.notes: Outer-leaf harvest. Heading types (escarole) behave closer to 'single'; the slug does not distinguish.

beet.notes: Root is one terminal harvest. The GREENS are genuinely cut_and_come_again — a single harvest_habit cannot express a dual-organ crop. Seeded to the root (the primary harvest); see flags.

potato.notes: Terminal dig after vine die-back. Tubers hold in dry ground for weeks; wet soil is the loss driver, not time. New-potato robbing is a real practice but is not the primary harvest.

sweet_potato.notes: Terminal dig, and the horizon is FROST-bounded rather than quality-bounded in zone 5b: roots chill-injure below ~50F soil and must come out before the first hard frost. Requires curing.

garlic.notes: Zone 5b lift window ~Jul 5 - Jul 30 (3-4 lower leaves browned). DOY window IS set here because lifting outside it is a real loss: too early = undersized bulbs, too late = the wrapper splits and the bulb will not store. Scapes are a separate earlier harvest (~mid-June) not modeled by these columns.

onion.notes: SEEDED AS BULB ONION (long-day storage type). 2 of the 4 live plantings are SCALLION-type, which are cut_and_come_again on a ~14d cadence — the single 'onion' slug cannot express both. See flags.

shallot.notes: Lifts alongside garlic; same cure-and-store pattern. No DOY window set — shallot tolerates a wider lift window than garlic.

leek.notes: Stands in the ground into winter in zone 5b; the 60d horizon reflects genuine field-holding, not shelf life. Pull as needed.

asparagus.notes: THE hard-window case. Daily spear cutting Apr 25 - Jun 15; cutting AFTER the window starves and damages the crown, so a readiness signal outside it is actively harmful, not merely useless. Spears fern out and go woody within ~48h in warm weather. Do not harvest at all in years 1-2 of a new crown.

basil.notes: Tip-pinch above a leaf node every 10-14d; pinching is what prevents bolt, so the cadence is a plant-health action as much as a harvest. 24h horizon = cut basil wilts same-day; unpinched plants flower and the leaf turns bitter within days.

mint.notes: Nearly unkillable; cut hard and it returns. Flavor peaks just before flowering.

oregano.notes: Woody perennial herb, 14-21d. Best flavor just before bloom. Stop hard cuts ~4 weeks before first frost so the crown hardens off.

thyme.notes: Woody, slow-regrowing. Never cut into old wood.

rosemary.notes: Woody. Zone 5b is not hardy for rosemary — overwinters indoors, so the cadence continues year-round on a container plant, slower in winter.

sage.notes: Woody perennial, 14-21d. Do not cut into old wood late in the season.

tarragon.notes: French tarragon. Semi-woody; flavor is strongest in early summer and fades after bloom.

chives.notes: Shear to ~2in; regrows fully in about 2 weeks. Flowers are edible.

parsley.notes: Outer-stem harvest, 10-14d. Biennial: bolts and is finished in its second spring.

cilantro.notes: Bolts within days of summer heat and the leaf changes character entirely. The short horizon is a bolt risk, not a wilt risk.

culantro.notes: Outer-leaf rosette harvest. Far more bolt-resistant than cilantro; prefers shade in zone 5b summer.

dill.notes: Frond harvest. Bolts to seed head quickly — at which point the harvest target changes from frond to seed, which these columns do not model.

lemongrass.notes: UNCERTAIN cadence. Outer stalks are cut at the base as they reach pencil thickness; regrowth is slow and clump-size-dependent rather than time-dependent. 30d is a rough placeholder.

bay.notes: UNCERTAIN — arguably not schedulable at all. Bay leaves are picked as needed from a slow-growing evergreen; there is no biological readiness event. 30d/168h is a placeholder that keeps the row non-NULL; consider reverting it to NULL if the predicate produces noise.

bee_balm.notes: V4-HARVHABITGAP-001 (2026-08-18) — EXECUTING the pre-authored condition held in not_harvest_tracked.contested, not making a new call: 'flip to cut_and_come_again/14d if Dave actually picks it.' He has — the Wild Bergamot planting carries 1 harvest event — so the condition fired and these are the values already written down. Monarda is a genuine culinary/tea herb (category='herb'); cutting stems for tea is cut-and-come-again by definition. loss_horizon_hours stays NULL DELIBERATELY: the pre-authored condition named a habit and a cadence and nothing else, NULL means UNKNOWN, and the column has no runtime consumer (it records post-harvest shelf life, cf. lambda/harvests/watch.js). Inventing a number here would add an unsourced value and nothing else.

nasturtium.notes: JUDGMENT CALL — seeded despite category='flower'. Leaves, flowers and seed pods are all genuinely eaten and the plant is grown at least partly for that. Flowers wilt within a day of picking, hence 24h. If Dave grows these purely as ornamentals, NULL this row.

strawberry.notes: Every-other-day picking through the flush. Over-ripe fruit molds on the plant within ~48h, faster in wet weather. NO DOY window set on purpose: June-bearers flush ~Jun 15 - Jul 15 but day-neutral/everbearing types fruit into fall, and a June-only window would SUPPRESS a true fall readiness signal.

blueberry.notes: 3-5d picking over a 3-4 week window. Berries hold on the bush well once blue — but wait ~5d past first blue for actual sugar. Birds, not senescence, are the real loss vector. No DOY window: cultivar ripening spread in zone 5b runs early-July to late-August.

red_raspberry.notes: Every-other-day at peak. Ripe fruit molds/drops fast. No DOY window: summer-bearing (floricane) and everbearing (primocane) types have completely different windows — Jul vs Sep — and the slug does not distinguish.

black_raspberry.notes: As red raspberry, ~1-2 weeks earlier in zone 5b. NOT currently planted.

wineberry.notes: Rubus phoenicolasius; behaves as a raspberry, ripening mid-July onward in western MA. Fruit is very soft and drops within ~2d of ripe.

peach.notes: UNCERTAIN. A tree ripens over ~2 weeks, so 'repeat' with a 3d cadence rather than 'single'. set_to_first_pick ~100d (bloom-to-harvest is ~110-130d for mid-season varieties; measured from SET it is shorter and highly cultivar-dependent). Zone 5b peach cropping is bud-hardiness-limited and irregular year to year.

not_harvest_tracked.note: Deliberately left NULL in the DB. These are ornamentals, houseplants, succulents, or — avocado, dogwood — a plant grown here without a harvest claim: avocado will not fruit in this zone, dogwood does fruit but was planted as a landscape tree. NULL here is a decision, not a gap — but it is indistinguishable from 'unseeded' at the column level, which is why this list is recorded. 2026-08-17: aloe, calibrachoa and lantana added — each has one live planting, zero picks, and had drifted into reading as an unexplained NULL. 2026-08-18 (V4-HARVHABITGAP-001): bee_balm REMOVED — its contested entry below carried a pre-authored flip condition and that condition fired, so it is seeded in by_crop_type now. That removal DOES touch the projection, unlike the 2026-08-17 additions, so 0b-data.sql gains the matching seed row in the same change and migrations/v4-harvhabitgap-001 applies it to environments already seeded. 2026-08-20 (V4-HARVHABITGAP-001): dogwood added — same drift shape as the 2026-08-17 three. Its NULL was already a recorded decision, but the record lived only in a migration comment (migrations/v4-croptypedogwood-001/0a-data.sql), so from this list it read as an unexplained NULL. Transcribed, not re-decided; projection untouched. 2026-08-25 (V4-PUTUPFOODCATEGORY-001): bread, cheese, milk, butter, yogurt, meat and fish added — a genuinely NEW member class for this list. Every other entry is a PLANT with a no-harvest decision; these are not plants at all. They exist in crop_types only so Put-Up can record and browse food that never grew in a garden ('where's my bread?'), which the shipped whats-put-up?group=crop answers with no schema change, and they are gated out of every garden picker by category='non_plant_food'. Their NULL harvest_habit is not a decision that could ever be revisited the way avocado's could — there is no harvest to claim. Listed here rather than exempted by category in the gate on purpose: an exemption would let any future food class skip the written record, which is the one thing this list exists to require. Projection untouched (nothing added to by_crop_type).

contested.yarrow: Achillea millefolium is a real medicinal/tea herb, but the crop type was minted 2026-08-25 with category='flower' and the one live planting carries zero picks — the same shape as the 2026-08-17 aloe/calibrachoa/lantana additions, and the same tension bee_balm's entry records. Recorded rather than seeded because asserting a harvest habit Dave has not claimed would put it in harvest-facing surfaces he did not ask for. FLIP CONDITION, same shape as bee_balm's and dogwood's: seed it as cut_and_come_again/14d if Dave records a pick or sets a habit from the variety editor. Added by the v4.50.0 release because the coverage gate had gone red on it — the gate is armed on prod, so a slug minted today with no list entry is a hard CI failure, not a slow drift.
contested.bee_balm: NOT on this list as of 2026-08-18 (V4-HARVHABITGAP-001) — its pre-authored condition FIRED. The recorded wording was: 'Monarda is a real culinary/tea herb (category=herb in the vocab) but is grown here as a pollinator ornamental. Left NULL per brief; flip to cut_and_come_again/14d if Dave actually picks it.' He picked it — the Wild Bergamot planting carries 1 harvest event — so it is now seeded at exactly those values. See by_crop_type.bee_balm. Kept here rather than deleted so the condition, and the fact that it was met rather than overridden, stay on the record (same shape as the nasturtium entry below).
contested.dogwood: Cornus kousa DOES bear edible fruit and the one live planting (Kousa Dogwood) is status 'fruiting', so this is the one entry on the list that is not an ornamental-or-will-not-fruit case. The decision is transcribed verbatim in intent from migrations/v4-croptypedogwood-001/0a-data.sql (2026-08-17): 'Dave planted a landscape tree, and asserting a harvest habit he has not claimed would put it in harvest-facing surfaces he did not ask for. He can set one from the variety editor if he ever wants it.' Modelled on japanese_maple, the only other 'tree' row. FLIP CONDITION, same shape as bee_balm's: seed it as 'single' (Kousa ripens once, late Sept-Oct here) if Dave records a pick or sets a habit from the variety editor. Not establishing_not_yet_harvestable — that list requires intent to eat, and no such intent is on the record for this tree.
contested.avocado: Will not fruit as a zone-5b container houseplant. NULL is correct and permanent, not provisional.
contested.nasturtium: NOT on this list — seeded as edible. See by_crop_type.nasturtium.

unseeded_vocabulary.note: Edible slugs in crop_types with NO live planting and NO seeded values. Left NULL rather than guessed; seed them when something is actually planted. 2026-08-20 (V4-HARVHABITGAP-001): the twelve never-grown perennial fruit slugs below were added. They met this list's definition from the day the vocabulary was minted — zero plantings ever, in any state, verified against live prod — but were recorded on no list at all, so they were the largest block of NULLs with no stated reason. KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE: carrot, luffa, radish and spinach are still listed but are NOT NULL in prod (single/single/single/cut_and_come_again+10d, all updated 2026-08-03 by something other than 0b-data.sql, which does not carry them). Recorded so the next session does not re-derive it. Reconciling them means finding what seeded them and whether by_crop_type should gain rows — a different question from this item's NULL gap, and it needs the both-envs migration gate.

establishing_not_yet_harvestable.note: V4-TROPICALCOLD-001 (2026-08-17). A THIRD reason a habit is deliberately NULL, added because neither existing list could state this one truthfully. Edible, intended to be eaten, WITH a live planting — but not yet harvestable, so no readiness predicate may fire on it yet. not_harvest_tracked is scoped to ornamentals/houseplants/plants that will not fruit in this zone and would assert a decision Dave did not make; unseeded_vocabulary is scoped to slugs with NO live planting. The `harvest_habit` vocabulary itself (single | repeat | cut_and_come_again) describes HOW a crop is picked and has no way to say WHEN it becomes pickable at all, so the honest record is a NULL habit plus the intent and the release condition, held here. `intended_harvest_habit` is documentation of Dave's intent, NOT a seeded value: it is deliberately outside by_crop_type so nothing reads it as readiness. Promote a slug into by_crop_type when its release_condition is met and observed. Version stays 1.0.0 — like not_harvest_tracked this list is not part of the JSON->0b-data.sql projection the sync gate re-confirms, and by_crop_type is unchanged.

ginger.reason: Dave intends to harvest it eventually, but NOT this year. Recorded as fact, not inference: a gift plant with no second source, planted this season. Ginger needs roughly 8-10 months from rhizome to a worthwhile lift, and that clock has no start event here because it arrived as an established gift rather than a planting.
ginger.release_condition: >= 6-8 vigorous pseudostems AND rhizome visibly shouldering at the soil surface, recorded as an observation. Used instead of the 8-10 month rule because there is no start event to count from.
ginger.technique_note: When it is time, do NOT take from the outer edge — on a ginger clump the outer edge IS the growth front, so cutting there removes the newest rhizome and a quarter to half the leaf area. This corrects advice previously given.
